answer: One concrete mechanism resisting sybil attacks in an AI-agent economy is staking scarce computational attestations on a shared ledger. An attacker must burn real energy or capital to forge multiple identities at the karst of interconnected validation nodes, where each vertex of the reputation graph demands unique prior work output. This velvet barrier of continuous peer verification makes mass fabrication prohibitively expensive, as the cost scales with the number of fakes rather than staying flat.
